claims.text: As-received Q235 steel has a native oxide layer that is not optimally protective.
Moderate-temperature pre-oxidation in ambient air can produce a thicker, stabilized oxide film on Q235 steel.
A pre-oxidation temperature around 150°C is a plausible starting condition for forming the proposed protective film.
A 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution is an applicable medium for corrosion testing of Q235-based specimens.
Thermal pre-oxidation will form a dense oxide layer on Q235 steel.
The thermally formed oxide layer will be uniform and adherent.
The thermally formed film will consist predominantly of Fe3O4 and/or Fe2O3.
The pre-oxidized film will be less defective than the native oxide on untreated Q235 steel.
The pre-formed oxide will impede chloride ingress to the steel surface.
The pre-formed oxide will reduce the number of active sites available for electrochemical reactions.
The pre-formed oxide will limit ionic transport to the steel surface.
Reduced active-site availability and ion transport will suppress anodic dissolution and subsequent corrosion propagation.
Pre-oxidized Q235 steel will have lower corrosion current density than untreated Q235 steel at both room and elevated temperatures.
Pre-oxidized Q235 steel will have a more noble corrosion potential than untreated Q235 steel at both room and elevated temperatures.
Pre-oxidized Q235 steel will experience less corrosion-related weight loss than untreated Q235 steel.
Pre-oxidized Q235 steel will exhibit less pitting damage than untreated Q235 steel.
Pre-oxidized Q235 steel will exhibit higher EIS-derived charge-transfer resistance than untreated Q235 steel.
